top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson is the only writer in the slate (P001), and I rank her above no award on literary grounds, not on the agreement recorded in earlier rounds. Her voice is recognisable in a few lines: cool, compressed, abrupt and exposed in feeling. Her formal achievement is substantial. Autobiography of Red turns the Geryon material into a verse novel, and Nox makes an elegy from translation, commentary and archival fragments, so the form carries the grief. The same concerns (loss, desire, inheritance, the limits of translation) recur across lyric, essay, verse narrative, drama and versions from Greek, which reads as one project. The citation should credit her original writing, with translation counted as method in Nox, and should not read as a prize for erudition. The maturity question stays open. I cannot verify from public knowledge whether the work after Nox deepens the project or refines a settled method, and the citation should not claim a late phase. My knowledge of the corpus is general and unverified, and her effects depend partly on typography and allusion that may travel unevenly into Swedish. These reservations lower my confidence but do not outweigh the case for the demonstrated core, so I rank P001 above P000.
